_doc: Preseason calendars found by hand, because probing could never have reached them. Every entry here is a page the hunter looked for and missed, and the reason is never the content: presaison.lnb.info and padlet.com are not on the league's own origin, so an origin probe cannot see them; tickets.vtb-league.com is a ticket seller, which sources.json already names as the category that publishes a draw first. A pinned URL is read every run and is NOT put to the looksLikeCalendar test — that gate exists to keep the hunter from adopting junk it found on its own, and a page a human vouched for has already passed a better one. Add a line here whenever you find one. A pin marked browser:true is left to render.mjs: a plain fetch returns an empty shell for it, so the hunter skips it rather than spending a read on 75 characters.

pinned.note: Official Spanish preseason table, all 16 clubs. Renders every column but the date; the dates come out of the page payload.
Official French preseason results and programme. On lnb.info, not lnb.fr.
VTB Super Cup group stage, 17-20 September, VTB Arena.

Israeli Premier League preseason, from the league's own board. cYear names the season in the page title but does NOT filter this list — 2025, 2026 and 2027 all return the same current fixtures. Games are added to it through the preseason, which is what a pin is for: it is re-read every run.
Italian preseason for all 16 clubs. Body is client-rendered — needs the browser layer.
German preseason board. A padlet, so client-rendered — needs the browser layer.

pinned.note: A broadcast schedule, which is a source of a kind this had none of: the channel showing a game almost never appears in the report announcing it. Rendered, because the page fetches at 66KB and 60 characters of text. Covers every sport, and its basketball rows say so — 'משחק הכנה בכדורסל: הפועל תל אביב - בלקן סופיה'. The channel is named once at the top of its own schedule rather than on each row, so it rides on the pin as `broadcaster`.

_broadcaster: A pin carrying `broadcaster` is that channel's own schedule: every game listed on it is shown by it, and the name is attached to rows that do not carry one themselves.
